prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create ONE circular illustration for the same growing early Earth shown in the reference icons. Original astronomical chromolithograph with chalk and dry gouache grain, midnight indigo circular field, ONE thin ivory rim, transparent exterior, square canvas. Reference 1 supplies the cutaway arrangement, reference 2 the same world's charcoal basalt skin and amber-orange cracks, reference 3 the angular pale-veined rock texture. These are style and material references, not elements to collage.
Subject: Proto-Earth with newly accreted hydrogen-bearing rocky material, before the separately represented metal-rich fragments arrive. A single approximately spherical dark charcoal growing world, with a modest wedge cutaway on the RIGHT. The outer basalt crust has irregular amber fissures. Inside the cutaway, show three or four distinguishable angular grey-brown rock clasts with thin pale grey mineral veins, embedded in darker fractured rock with a restrained warm orange glow between fractures. Keep the clasts visibly STONY, not shiny round metallic blobs. Most of the exterior silhouette remains intact. View matches the metal-bearing-Earth cutaway reference; the new interior is rocky rather than a collection of silver metal droplets. No polished central metal ball, no separate second planet. No ocean, liquid water, droplets, blue pools, atmosphere or ice; the hydrogen is carried chemically in rock, and its precise identity will be supplied by the normal item name. Do not claim to depict molecules. No labels, text, symbols, arrows, machinery, life or familiar continents. Strong simple masses must read at 72px. Circle occupies about92% of square width; generous transparent corners. Preserve the single pale rim and quiet dark field.
